story_text:
This is our digital instrument cluster for the BMW E30. It sits in the factory gauge pod, and from the driver's seat it reads like the gauges BMW put there, drawn on sharp modern displays.
Our cluster, powered on, in an original E30 cluster housing. This is a photograph of the real hardware, not a rendering.
This campaign funds Batch One, limited to 500 clusters for the E30 at $1,349 each, sold only here on Kickstarter. If we reach our goal, backers who choose an E30 Batch One reward receive a cluster from Batch One. Separate E28 and E36 tiers reserve places in future batches.
Batch One at a glance
- $1,349 per cluster, limited to 500 units, sold only on Kickstarter
- Fits: the BMW E30. Send us your year, model and a photo of your cluster, and we will confirm fit before you pledge
- Estimated delivery: shipping starts in October 2027
- Ships worldwide, with shipping charged after the campaign. Outside the United States, your cluster ships once radio certification for your country is complete
- Every unit serialized and tested before it ships
## What it is
Not So Classic Cluster replaces the gauges inside your E30's original binnacle with digital displays drawn to read like the factory dials. Everything you glance at while driving stays where your eyes expect it.
- What it shows. The cluster in our photos shows the speedometer, tachometer, fuel gauge and temperature gauge in their factory positions. On the shipping cluster: the same four gauges in the same positions, with a rolling digital odometer and trip meter in the speedometer, mph or km/h chosen when you first turn it on, and a coolant gauge that warns you in stages at set points you choose, plus the warning lights your factory cluster shows: turn signals, high beam, oil pressure, brake and charge. With a supported standalone engine computer on CAN, it can also show extra engine data such as boost, oil temperature and pressure, and ethanol content. MaxxECU is verified today; support for other popular engine computers still needs testing.
- Fits the factory gauge pod. It is designed around the E30's original binnacle, so the dash keeps its stock look. No tablet bolted to the dash.
- Reads like the original. The dial art is drawn to read like the factory gauges, not like a phone screen.
- Inside. Round digital displays, with WiFi and Bluetooth, plus a round display knob designed to sit where the factory on-board computer (OBC) or clock goes, in its own bezel. The knob also works as an extra gauge or a clock. Our new development displays run at 60 frames per second and are rated at 1,000 nits for daylight readability. The radios are there so planned features, such as updates and a phone app, can reach your cluster later without new hardware.
What's in the box
- One complete Not So Classic Cluster for the BMW E30, serialized and tested. You never send us your original cluster.
- The control knob in its own bezel, made to sit where your factory on-board computer (OBC) or clock goes
- Access to our step-by-step online E30 install guide, with photos
We are also working on features that are not finished yet. They are not part of what you are pledging for:
- Firmware updates over WiFi, Bluetooth or USB, with a fallback to the previous version if an update fails
- A phone app for setup
- A self-test screen that shows what every input is reading
- GPS-assisted speedometer calibration
If we ship any of these, backers will get them at no extra cost.
## Installing it in your E30
These are the first questions every E30 owner asks, so here are straight answers.
- How it connects: Batch One is designed to plug into your E30's original cluster connectors and to work with the stock engine computer, speed sensor and fuel level sender. No wiring is needed unless you add optional sensors. Our prototype is still wired by hand on the bench, and the production plug-in connection is part of the work this campaign funds.
- Install time: Because it plugs into the original connectors, installing it should be about as involved as removing and refitting a factory E30 cluster, which most owners do at home with basic hand tools, plus fitting the knob. We will publish a measured time once we have installed production units.
- Going back to stock: Yes. You keep your original cluster, so going back means plugging it back in and refitting your on-board computer or clock.
Before Batch One ships, we will publish a step-by-step E30 install guide with photos of the actual connectors.
## Where it stands today
We would rather show you the real state of the project than a polished promise.
What exists now:
- A working cluster that has been driven on the road in Jean's BMW E28, which runs a MaxxECU engine computer (first drive in September 2026). Our E30 test car is not ready to drive yet.
- A bench prototype we use for development.
- The video at the top of this page is real prototype footage, filmed in October 2026, and every photo of the cluster shows the actual hardware. None are renderings. Features the video marks as in development are not part of what you are pledging for.
[画像: Not So Classic Cluster prototype on the bench in an original BMW E30 cluster housing]
Above: the prototype on our bench, built into an original E30 cluster housing.
What is still to do before Batch One ships:
- Finish the production files for the main cluster board.
- Finish the production firmware for the E30.
- Bench and in-car testing, including the conditions a cluster actually lives with: heat soak on a dashboard in the Florida sun, vibration, a sensor that opens or shorts, the voltage dip while the engine cranks, and electrical spikes on a 12V system.
- Revise the design based on what testing finds.
- Radio certification. Because the cluster has WiFi and Bluetooth, it needs FCC certification before it can be sold in the United States, and its own radio approval in each other country we ship to. Nothing ships to a country until its certification is done.
- A written build procedure and a production test, so every unit is built the same way and checked before it leaves.
We track each cluster we develop on a seven-stage roadmap: In research, In design, Prototyping, In testing, In revision, Pre-production and In production. Today the E30 cluster is In testing, step 4 of 7. We report progress as a step on that roadmap rather than a percentage, and we will post an update every time the E30 cluster moves forward.
## What your pledge does
Your pledge turns a working prototype into finished, tested clusters. It pays for:
- Production engineering. Finishing the main cluster board files and the production firmware.
- Testing. Bench and in-car testing, and the design changes that come out of it.
- Certification. FCC radio certification, the radio approvals for other countries, and the lab fees that come with them.
- Manufacturing. Circuit boards, displays, enclosures and assembly for every Batch One cluster backed here, up to 500.
- Quality and traceability. A serial number and a functional test for every unit before it ships.
- Packaging and fulfillment. Protective packaging for the displays, and packing and dispatch to backers.
Estimated delivery: we expect to start shipping in October 2027. Batch One will ship in stages as units are completed and tested; some units may ship after October. That estimate includes time for testing, FCC certification, parts and assembly, plus a cushion. We will post an update as each item on our still-to-do list is completed, and regular updates in between, even when the news is that nothing has changed. If something slips, you will hear it from us first, with the reason and a new estimate.
During the campaign, the cluster is available only here. It is not for sale on our website while the campaign runs. After the campaign ends, the next batch will be sold on our website at or above the Kickstarter price, so backers will not see the same cluster offered for less right after backing it.
## Why we built it
The youngest E30s are more than thirty years old and the oldest are past forty, and so are their instruments. Owners who want better information from their car have usually had two choices: keep the original cluster as it is, or add a screen or a row of aftermarket gauges somewhere they were never meant to go. Neither feels right in a car people have spent years getting exactly right.
We think a modern display should earn its place in a classic by respecting it. That means sitting in the original binnacle, reading at a glance the way the factory dials do, and looking like it came with the car. Open the door and it should look like an E30. Turn the key and it should feel like one, only sharper.
The idea started in Jean's restoration shop, The Usual Suspects Garage in Naples, Florida, where classic BMWs and Porsches are the daily work. It started out under the name Classic Dash, which you may also see on our website. It is now a product of its own, and this campaign is how we build the first batch.
## Who we are
We are two people, and we split the work cleanly.
Jean Stanis, CEO, handles the product and the build. The cluster was developed in Jean's shop, alongside the cars it is meant for. Jean designs the cluster's gauge faces and leads its hardware and firmware. The shop also repairs wiring harnesses and builds custom ones, including harnesses for standalone engine computers.
David Tanis, COO, handles the business side: the website, backer communication and customer support. When you write to us, David answers.
We have filed to form NS Classic Cluster, LLC, a Florida company, to make, sell and support the cluster. Our ambition is not a garage add-on. It is a real product, built in the hundreds, that ends up in your car and works there.
## Beyond the E30
The E30 is first. The complete cluster rewards in this campaign are for the E30; separate E28 and E36 tiers reserve places in future batches and do not include a complete cluster. Their full prices, fitment and hardware delivery dates are not yet confirmed. Each reservation is $100, credited in full toward the selected model, and refundable until the remaining balance is paid. There are 100 reservation spots per model. January 2027 refers to the digital reservation confirmation only. Batch One comes first, and work on the next car will not take priority over delivering it.
Our plan is a single firmware with a settings profile for each car, so the clusters that follow the E30 can share the same foundation. Clusters for the BMW E28 (with layouts for the E23 and E24) and the Porsche 930 and 964 are also in development, and the BMW E21, E36, E34 and E32 are planned for a later round. Each one needs its own dial art, its own sender calibration and possibly its own wiring, which is why we build them one at a time.
Tell us what you drive. Backers can post in the comments, and anyone can let us know at notsoclassiccluster.com. Owner interest helps us decide which car comes next.
## Thank you
We built this because we wanted it to exist, and because we think the people who keep these cars alive deserve instruments made with the same care they put into everything else. If that sounds like you, back Batch One, share this page with an E30 owner you know, and follow along. We will show you every step.
Jean and David
Not So Classic Cluster is an independent product and is not affiliated with or endorsed by BMW AG or Porsche AG. BMW and Porsche are trademarks of their respective owners, and model names are used only to describe fitment.
risks: Shipping automotive hardware is hard, and we are a two-person team. A working cluster in a real car is a strong start, but it is not the same thing as 500 finished units. Here is what we see, and what we are doing about it. Manufacturing. The production files for the main cluster board are not finished yet, and today Jean is the one who builds the cluster. Before Batch One we will finish those files, run a pre-production batch and write a build procedure, so every unit is built the same way. The circuit boards will be made and assembled by a professional board manufacturer, and final assembly and testing of every cluster will happen at our shop in Naples. Components. Lead times for displays, chips and boards set our delivery window, and some parts may have only one source. We are confirming lead times for every major part before launch, and our estimated delivery is built on them. If a part slips, we will tell you in an update, with the reason and a new estimate. Certification. The cluster has WiFi and Bluetooth, so it needs FCC certification before it can be sold in the United States, and a separate radio approval for each other country or region we ship to, such as Canada, the European Union, the United Kingdom and Australia. Certification is done on a specific hardware and firmware configuration, and a failed test means a design change and a retest. That is the main reason our estimated delivery has room in it. Nothing ships to a country until its certification is complete, so backers outside the United States may receive their clusters after US backers. Firmware. The production firmware for the E30 is still being finished. Features we list as planned, such as updates, the phone app and the self-test screen, are not part of what you are pledging for. Installation and legal requirements. Cars differ, and so do their senders and wiring. The "Installing it in your E30" section above explains what installation involves, and a step-by-step E30 install guide with connector photos will be published before Batch One ships. A replacement cluster also has to show the required warning indicators, such as turn signals and high beam, and handle the odometer correctly. Our cluster will show the turn signal and high beam indicators, along with the other warning lights the factory cluster shows. Before anything ships, both will be reviewed against the rules for replacement clusters. Support and fulfillment. David answers every message, and we record the serial number and firmware version of every unit we ship so we can help with your exact cluster. Packing and shipping clusters with glass displays is real work: David is responsible for fulfillment, and every cluster is packed and shipped from our shop in Naples, Florida. Timeline. Our estimated delivery is an estimate, not a firm ship date, built with room for testing, certification and manufacturing. If it moves, you will hear it from us first, with the reason. faq.q: When will Batch One start shipping?
faq.a: We expect the first units to start shipping in October 2027. Batch One will ship in stages as units are completed and tested; some units may ship after October. Timing is estimated, subject to testing, certification, component lead times and assembly. International delivery may follow US delivery while the required radio approvals are completed. If the schedule changes, we will explain why and provide an updated estimate.

The complete cluster rewards in this campaign are for the BMW E30. Before you pledge for an E30 cluster, send us your car's year and model and a photograph of its cluster so we can confirm fitment. Separate $100 E28 and E36 reservation tiers reserve places in future batches; they do not include a complete cluster. Fitment, full pricing and hardware delivery dates for those models are still to be confirmed. Other BMW and Porsche models remain future projects.

faq.q: What warranty and repair support are planned?
faq.a: Every cluster comes with a two-year warranty against defects in parts and workmanship. We will offer repairs for at least five years. Every unit is serialized, and we record its firmware version so we can support your exact cluster. Contact us through Kickstarter if you need help.

faq.q: Are the phone app and wireless updates included in my pledge?
faq.a: No. Firmware updates over WiFi, Bluetooth or USB, a phone app, a self-test screen and GPS-assisted speedometer calibration are still in development. They are not part of what you are pledging for. If we ship these features, backers will receive them at no extra cost.
